_about: Which sections of which law govern a question about a floorplan. Hand-kept; every citation is checked against the text in this repo and the tool says so when one is missing. These are pointers to the law to read, not a code check: the Multiple Dwelling Law and the Housing Maintenance Code in particular depend on when the building was erected and its class, so read each section's applicability paragraph.

rooftop structures.question: What may go on a roof (bulkheads, penthouses, decks) without counting as a story or floor area?
rooftop structures.note: Zoning and the Building Code ask different questions. Zoning asks whether the structure penetrates the height limit or adds floor area; the Building Code asks whether it adds a story or height under Table 504.3 and how it must be built.

cites.why: the Building Code's definition: an enclosed rooftop structure sheltering a shaft, stair, tank or equipment, not for human occupancy
the companion definition: an enclosed rooftop structure designed or used for human occupancy

Exception 1: rooftop structures (tanks, mechanical equipment, bulkheads, penthouses, greenhouses, chimneys) count as neither building height nor a story while their aggregate area is 33 1/3 percent of the roof or less
rooftop structures are governed by Section 1510 and stay subject to the Chapter 5 roof-coverage and height limits
construction type for bulkheads and penthouses, relaxed when all rooftop structures stay within 33 1/3 percent of the roof
penthouse walls and roofs follow Tables 601 and 602 for the building's construction class
a bulkhead may shelter only mechanical equipment or shaft openings, with louvers or flashing against the weather
buildings over 22 feet with a low-slope roof need a 42-inch parapet, guard or fence, which may sit up to 6 feet in from the wall
antenna supports, flagpoles, drying frames, duckboarding and decking or platforms covering up to 20 percent of the roof may be combustible if under 12 feet high
buildings of four or more stories or over 40 feet need a stair to the roof through a bulkhead complying with 1510.2
zoning floor area counts floor space in penthouses but excludes elevator or stair bulkheads, water tanks and cooling towers (except in R2A)

paragraph (c): elevator and stair bulkheads, tanks and mechanical equipment may penetrate the height limit, set back from the street wall, within 50 or 30 percent of the building's lot coverage and 15, 25, 35 or 55 feet above the permitted height
the maximum base and building heights in R6 through R12 districts that those obstructions are measured above
the Multiple Dwelling Law reaches only multiple dwellings, three or more families living independently; one- and two-family houses are outside it
